title: LSTM state carried through each trial
description: The network runs through each training trial in time order (all session-1 trials side by side), and its hidden and cell state passes from one 200 ms chunk to the next instead of restarting at zero. Every sample is a target; gradients span one chunk; the state restarts at each trial. Test trials run once from start to end. Scored on the same samples as the reference. Everything else as the reference: Active torque (each session's own relaxed-hold passive torque subtracted), EMG ÷ session-1 maximum, no per-angle loss scaling (plain mean-squared error, every angle weighted by its own torque), LSTM 16 units × 2 layers, dropout 0.0, learning rate 0.01 (chosen by a validation-loss search), trained with batch 64 for at most 150 epochs (fast protocol: learning rate × 0.5 after 6 flat epochs, early stop 15, at most 150 epochs), trained on session 1 and tested on session 2, 6 people × 10 seeds. The EMG envelope is causal (forward-only filters: no input uses later EMG, as in a real-time device; 2nd-order 2 Hz low-pass, about 125 ms lag) and the first and last 1 s of every trial are cut. Batch size does not apply here: the 8 session-1 trials always train side by side; the learning-rate schedule and early stopping follow the fast protocol. Validation windows start one window span after the training part of each trial, so no validation window reuses training inputs (purged split). Training windows are fed in time order (no shuffling).
